# Wickra Terminal

> A streaming trading terminal built on the Wickra core — live charts, order-book, tape and 455 streaming indicators — with a native TUI and a Web front-end as two renderers over the same logic. One data-driven core, N front-ends, in ten languages, deterministic and byte-identical across every binding.

Wickra Terminal is a streaming trading terminal with one data-driven core (`terminal-core`) that folds market events into an O(1) `AppState` and turns panels into view-models (values, series, colours) — never renderer commands. The native TUI maps a view-model to a ratatui widget; the Web app maps the same view-model to a canvas draw; they are separate programs rather than two modes of one binary. Data arrives through a `DataSource` trait with four activatable modules: `Live` (the wickra-exchange connectivity layer over the ten largest venues), `Replay` (a recorded feed with time-machine seek), `Manual` (host-fed, which is how the browser bridges its own WebSocket), and `Synth` (a deterministic synthetic feed). The core is exposed as a JSON-over-C-ABI data API (`Terminal::command_json`) in Rust, Python, Node.js, WASM and — over a C ABI — C, C++, C#, Go, Java and R, so a developer in any language builds their own front-end on the same core. Released under the MIT OR Apache-2.0 license.

- [Benchmarks](https://terminal.wickra.org/benchmarks): What the core costs per tick.

## Related
